summary: 5. Thus, the statutory changes brought about by the said GOI notifications dated 17.9.2025, squarely fall within the ambit of a change in law event, applicable to all PPAs having a composite scheme and covered under Section 63 of the Act. Hence, there was a need to issue a uniform regulatory direction for a consistent treatment of the change in law events (due to notifications dated 17.9.2025) and to facilitate the settlement of the dues on account of such change in law events, across the PPAs regulated by this Commission, including the tariff framework, with effect from 22.9.2025. In this backdrop, the Commission initiated Suo motu proceedings (in Petition No.10/SM/2025) and, vide order dated 1.10.2025, issued a public notice with directions to the parties to file their written submissions. The petition was listed for a public hearing on 14.10.2025. 6. During the hearing of the said petition on 14.10.2025, the learned counsels appearing for some of the generators viz., GMR Warora Energy Ltd (GMRWEL), GMR Kamalanga Energy Ltd (GMRKEL), Jindal India Power Ltd (JIPL), Jhabua Power Ltd (JPL), SEIL Energy India Ltd (SEIL) and MB Power Limited (MBPL) and the representatives /learned counsels appearing for some of the Distribution companies, namely Tamil Nadu Power Development Corporation Ltd (TNPDCL) and MSEDCL made oral submissions, and a few other Discoms have filed their submissions in terms of the directions of the Commission in an order dated 1.10.2025. The party-wise submissions made during the public hearing, including the written submissions filed by them, are (g) The continuation of the previously approved methodology will ensure regulatory consistency, avoid unnecessary duplication of proceedings, and facilitate timely and efficient reconciliation of claims between the contracting parties. (h) The Commission may direct that, for such PPAs where a change in law mechanism already exists and has been implemented pursuant to earlier orders of this Commission, the same methodology shall be applicable for the present change in law event, unless otherwise specifically directed by the Commission. Any dispute pertaining to the compensation will be decided on a case-by-case basis. (i) The Commission ought to provide leeway to permit parties to approach basis individual PPAs, otherwise, it would lead to unnecessary litigations, which is being sought to be avoided (a) PPAs entered into between generating companies and distribution licensees/trading intermediaries largely contain provisions in relation to change in law events, which are restitutive in nature, with the aim of ensuring that the affected party is restored to the same economic position as if such change in law has not occurred. The Hon’ble Supreme Court has held that the purpose of compensating the party affected by change in law events through monthly tariff payments in order to restore such affected party to the same economic position as if such change in law event had not occurred, i.e., the affected party must be given the benefit of restitution as understood in civil law. (Judgment in UHBVNL v AP(M)L (2023 2 SCC 624) and UHBVNL v APL (2019 5 SCC 325) relied upon. (b) Keeping the principles of restitution in mind, it would be apposite for this Commission to devise a compensation mechanism to ensure that only the actual impact of the Change in Law event ensures to the benefit of the affected party. Further, in order to ensure adequate stakeholder participation, this Commission may consider circulating/publishing the proposed compensation mechanism and invite stakeholder comments 7. As stated earlier, the Commission, after taking cognizance of the two notifications dated 17.9.2025 and keeping in view that the said notifications are change in law events, _suo motu_ proceedings have been initiated by this Commission, for arriving at a uniform regulatory direction for a consistent treatment of the change in law events and to facilitate the settlement of the dues due to such change in law events, across the PPAs regulated by this Commission under Section 63 of the Act and bidding guidelines of the Central Government, with effect from 22.9.2025. uniformity with our decision in Petition No. 13/SM/2017, we, in exercise of the regulatory powers under Section 79(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 direct that all the generating companies, shall compute the net impact of the above statutory changes on the landed coal cost, station-wise and month-wise, considering the increase in the rates of GST and the abolition of Compensation cess on the procurement of coal as observed by Commission in the previous paras. In this regard, the generators shall furnish to the Discoms/ Beneficiary States, the relevant details, backed by an Auditor’s certificate and the relevant documents, and accordingly, refund the amount(s) payable to the Discoms/ Beneficiaries, as a result of such a change in law event. Any difference between the provisional and the actual impact of the change in law events shall be reconciled between the parties and recovered in terms of the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021. However, in case of any dispute on any of the taxes, duties and cesses, the parties are at liberty to approach this Commission for redressal.
title: Abolition of GST Compensation Cess and increase in the GST rate on procurement of coal from 5% to 18%.
